Q: How to turn makefile into JSON Compilation Database? A:

I often work on Windows and needed a script to create compile_commands.json from a gcc build from STM32CubeIDE. The build-in option to generate the file did not work for me* so I wrote my own script.

I noticed some of the answers here have a lot of assumptions with regex. Such as that -c cannot occur on a line without a -c argument and that gcc cannot occur in a line other than a compile/link line. I'm using stricter forms of parsing.

Compile arguments can contain escaped strings and other complexities so I gave up on using regex. I decided to parse each line using shlex.

The generated file can be processed by clang-tidy. Only sysroots needed to be passed to clang-tidy to make it find system includes.

import subprocess
import json
import shlex
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

def abspath_from(base_dir, path):
    p = Path(path)
    return (p if p.is_absolute() else Path(base_dir) / p).resolve()

def generate_db(build_dir):
    lc = ["make", "all", "--always-make", "--dry-run"]

    result = subprocess.run(lc, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=build_dir, encoding="utf-8")

    retcode = result.returncode
    stdout_string = result.stdout   

    commands = []
    for line in stdout_string.splitlines():
        args = shlex.split(line)
        if args[0].endswith(("gcc","g++","clang","clang++","c++")) and "-c" in args:        
            file = str(abspath_from(build_dir,args[1])) # convert file to absolute path
            args[1] = '"' + file + '"' # path argument needs double quotes, json lib will escape them
            command = " ".join(args) # join updated args
            commands.append({"directory":".", "command": command, "file": file, "output":str(abspath_from(build_dir,args[-1]))})

    compile_commands_path = os.path.join(build_dir, "compile_commands.json")
    with open(compile_commands_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(commands, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) >= 2:
         build_dir = sys.argv[1]
    else:
         build_dir = '.'
   
    generate_db(build_dir)

*STM32CubeIDE can generate compile_commands.json, but it cannot save the setting in the project, only in workspace. So every developer has to manually check a box after cloning a project. Additionally it contains a bug. The paths are all relative to the build folder, but the directory field has the parent folder. This causes all include paths to fail. Setting directory to "." manually fixes this issue.

Q: Python layout: how to draw a box around a frame? A:

if you use PyQt then you may have to put QBoxLayout inside QFrame which may set frame with .setFrameShape() .setFrameShadow() .setLineWidth().

In this (old) documentation you can see image with different frames.

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QFrame, QLabel

app = QApplication([])

window = QWidget()
main_layout = QVBoxLayout(window)

frame = QFrame()
frame.setFrameShape(QFrame.Shape.Box)  # or Panel, StyledPanel, etc.
frame.setFrameShadow(QFrame.Shadow.Raised)
frame.setLineWidth(2)

frame_layout = QVBoxLayout(frame)
frame_layout.addWidget(QLabel("Item 1"))
frame_layout.addWidget(QLabel("Item 2"))

main_layout.addWidget(frame)

window.show()
app.exec()

Or put in QWidget which can use CSS to draw border (and it can have rounded corners).

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QLabel

app = QApplication([])

window = QWidget()
main_layout = QVBoxLayout(window)

frame = QWidget()

frame.setObjectName("box")  # to assign frame only to widget but not to children
frame.setStyleSheet(
    """
    QWidget#box {
        border: 2px solid black;
        border-radius: 6px;
    }
"""
)

layout = QVBoxLayout(frame)
layout.addWidget(QLabel("Item 1"))
layout.addWidget(QLabel("Item 2"))

main_layout.addWidget(frame)

window.show()
app.exec()

There is also QGroupBox which allows to add frame with title/header. But you can also set empty string and it will display only frame.

from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QWidget, QVBoxLayout, QFrame, QLabel
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QGroupBox

app = QApplication([])

window = QWidget()
main_layout = QVBoxLayout(window)

# group = QGroupBox("Settings")
group = QGroupBox("")

layout = QVBoxLayout(group)
layout.addWidget(QLabel("Option A"))
layout.addWidget(QLabel("Option B"))

main_layout.addWidget(group)

window.show()
app.exec()

Q: how to save the logs for docker-compose up -d --build A:

Since docker compose v2.19.0 --progress is now a global flag, so it can even be used for up like

docker compose --progress plain up --build

or just build:

docker compose --progress plain build

Then just pipe the output to a file with appendix > build.log

Now the --progress flag even gives you a deprecated warning when used after docker compose build

--progress is a global compose flag, better use `docker compose --progress xx build ...
